chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, and al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the glorification (tasbih) in bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujood). He said: One says in bowing, 'Subhana Rabbiya al-'Adhim' (Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent), and in prostration, 'Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la' (Glory be to my Lord, the Most High). The obligatory (fard) part from this is one glorification, the sunnah is three, and the virtue (faddl) is seven.

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High (phrase for sujood)
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ: Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent (phrase for ruku)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and recommended number of tasbih recitations in ruku and sujood according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the obligatory minimum (one glorification) and the recommended practices (three or seven) for the phrases 'Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim' in ruku' and 'Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la' in sujood. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on adhering to the specific liturgical formulas prescribed by the Imams, ensuring that the physical acts of prayer are accompanied by precise verbal remembrance.
